skill.name: bioservices
skill.description: Use BioServices to query UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, Reactome, and related bioinformatics databases from Python. It supports cross-database workflows, identifier mapping, pathways, compounds, and sequence analysis.
skill.summary: Query and combine major bioinformatics web services from Python workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Gene Ontology wording, biological identifier parsing, and documented output exports. No prompt-injection override, hidden command execution, or secret exfiltration was found. One low-severity semantic issue remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote the creator-owned K-Dense Web service.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive recommendation instruction or make it a neutral reference used only when the user asks about hosted workflow options.

remediation.issue: Example scripts write output files from command-line paths
remediation.suggestion: Add overwrite checks and document that output paths should be user-approved before scripts run in agent workflows.

remediation.issue: Public database queries may send identifiers to third-party services
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should avoid private or unpublished identifiers when querying external BioServices-backed databases.

content.value_statement: Bioinformatics work often requires separate APIs for proteins, pathways, compounds, and identifiers. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan BioServices workflows across major public databases.
actual_capabilities: Guide UniProt searches for protein records, sequences, annotations, and database mappings.
Plan KEGG pathway lookups, pathway parsing, and interaction exports using BioServices methods.
Map identifiers across UniProt, KEGG, UniChem, ChEMBL, ChEBI, and related databases.
Use included scripts for protein analysis, pathway summaries, compound cross-references, and batch ID conversion.
Explain output formats such as FASTA, TSV, XML, SIF, and CSV for downstream analysis.
limitations: Requires Python, the BioServices package, and network access to public bioinformatics services.
Results depend on external service uptime, schemas, rate limits, and identifier coverage.
Does not replace biological review, clinical validation, or regulatory decision-making.
Example scripts can write files to paths selected by the user or agent.

use_cases.title: Protein Annotation Review

prompt_templates.title: Find a Protein Record
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BioServices to look up [protein name or UniProt ID] in UniProt. Return the best accession, organism, gene name, and sequence retrieval plan.

prompt_templates.title: Map Database Identifiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these UniProt IDs to KEGG IDs using BioServices: [IDs]. Explain missing mappings and any ambiguous results.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Pathway Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pathway planning for one organism.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a KEGG pathway analysis for organism [code] and gene list [genes]. Include expected outputs, rate-limit precautions, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Multi-Service Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow design across several databases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a BioServices workflow that combines UniProt annotations, KEGG pathways, ChEMBL or ChEBI compound data, and PSICQUIC interactions for [research question].

output_examples.output: A concise UniProt-centered plan with accession lookup, FASTA retrieval, KEGG pathway mapping, and optional interaction database checks.

output_examples.input: Convert a list of UniProt accessions to KEGG identifiers.
output_examples.output: A mapping summary that separates successful conversions, missing IDs, and identifiers that require manual review.

output_examples.input: Cross-reference the compound Geldanamycin across public databases.
output_examples.output: A compound report with KEGG, ChEBI, and ChEMBL identifiers, plus notes about unavailable fields or service errors.

best_practices: Start with exact accessions, compound IDs, and organism codes whenever possible.
Cache intermediate results and respect public service rate limits during repeated queries.
Validate important mappings against source database pages before publishing results.
anti_patterns: Running broad searches without organism filters or known identifiers.
Treating automated database mappings as final biological evidence.
Sending private, unpublished, or regulated identifiers to public web services without approval.

faq.question: What is BioServices used for?
faq.answer: BioServices provides Python access to many biological databases, including UniProt, KEGG, ChEMBL, ChEBI, Reactome, and QuickGO.

faq.question: Does this skill run the database queries itself?
faq.answer: It guides BioServices workflows and includes example scripts. Actual queries require Python, BioServices, and network access.

faq.question: Can it convert identifiers between databases?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover mappings such as UniProt to KEGG and KEGG compounds to ChEMBL through UniChem.

faq.question: Can I use it for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. It is for research workflows and should not be used as clinical, diagnostic, or regulatory authority.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare known IDs, organism codes, accepted output paths, and a plan for validating results against source databases.
